question.prompt: A rhombus is inscribed in triangle \(ABC\) in such a way that one of its vertices is \(A\) and two of its sides lie along \(AB\) and \(AC.\) If \(AC=6\) inches, \(AB=12\) inches, and \(BC=8\) inches, the side of the rhombus, in inches, is:

solutions.explanation:
A rhombus has four equal sides and parallel opposite sides, so we can relate its side length to the triangle's sides without finding any angles.

Name the rhombus \(APQR\), with \(P\) on \(AB\), \(R\) on \(AC\), and its opposite vertex \(Q\) on \(BC\). Let its side length be \(s\). Then \(AP=PQ=s\), \(BP=12-s\), and \(PQ\parallel AC\).

A line parallel to one side of a triangle cuts off proportional corresponding sides. Applied in triangle \(BAC\), this gives
\[
\frac{PQ}{AC}=\frac{BP}{BA},
\qquad
\frac{s}{6}=\frac{12-s}{12}.
\]
Thus
\[
12s=72-6s,
\qquad 18s=72,
\qquad s=4.
\]
This is positive and less than both adjacent triangle sides, as required. The rhombus side is \(4\) inches, choice D.
solutions.title: Use the parallel sides
